subject: Nebula Systems — Dedicated capacity sizing questionnaire & GPU mix discussion
messages:
From: Susan Park <susan.park@nebulasystems.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: Ravi Patel <ravi.patel@nebulasystems.com>
Date: 2026-08-26T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity questionnaire — initial data request

Diego,

Thanks for taking this RFP. As part of our procurement we need a completed sizing workbook and some clarifications on GPU mix for different workload shapes. High level:

- Expected steady-state concurrent requests: 120 qps for text-generation (avg 200 tokens per request).
- Peak burst: 350 qps sustained for up to 15 minutes, 1–2x per day.
- Latency target: p95 < 250ms token latency, end-to-end response < 750ms for 200-token outputs.
- Workload mix: 70% streaming chat, 20% batch-embed, 10% reranking.
- Requirement: VPC private deployment, SOC2 evidence, and SLA for 99.9% availability.

Attached is our template (capacity_workbook.xlsx). Please return with recommended GPU types, node counts, and any multiplexing/tenant-packing guidance. Also flag any assumptions you make.

We'd like the workbook back by EOD Aug 29 if possible.

Thanks,
Susan Park
Sr. Procurement Manager
Nebula Systems
[attachment: capacity_workbook.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: Susan Park <susan.park@nebulasystems.com>
Cc: ava_chen@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-26T12:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity questionnaire — initial data request

Susan —

Appreciate the clear requirements and the workbook. We reviewed the workload sketch and sketched a conservative baseline plus two alternate packing strategies. High level answers here; I attached a filled workbook and a short PDF with assumptions.

Executive summary (details in attachments):
- Recommended baseline: 8 x H100 (80GB) nodes + 6 x A100-80GB nodes as a mixed pool. Rationale: H100 for low-tail-latency streaming, A100 for high-throughput batch and embedding pipelines.
- Burst model: add 6 pre-warmed A100 slots (burst pool) with autoscale trigger at 280 qps sustained over 30s.
- Multiplexing approach: tenant-aware packing with per-tenant memory quotas, modem-level KV cache sharing for common prefixes; expect 20–35% effective concurrency uplift vs 1:1 mapping.
- Quantization: int8/4 paths recommended for embedding jobs and reranking where small quality delta is acceptable. We recommend gating quantization with eval sets.
- SLA implementation: cross-region fallback to secondary pool in us-west/ us-east with automated model-fallback to a smaller variant (quantized A100) if primary capacity hits 95% for >120s.

Key assumptions (short):
- Average request size 200 tokens, median response 180 tokens after stop tokens.
- KV cache hit-rate assumed 18% for chat (based on initial prompt family).
- No heavy multimodal inference.

See attachments: diego_capacity_answers_v1.pdf (narrative + table) and the completed capacity_workbook.xlsx. We can walk through the workbook in a quick 30–45m call — ava and hannah are on this message to help with kernel selection and runbook details.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal technical sync (30m) with Nebula's infra/ML teams to confirm sequence-length distribution and caching prospects.
2) Final workbook delivery by Aug 29 after any adjustments from that sync.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Director, Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference
[attachment: diego_capacity_answers_v1.pdf (pdf)]

From: ava_chen@redwood.com
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-27T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: internal: GPU mix thoughts + latency SLO tradeoffs

Diego / Hannah —

Quick technical notes to support Diego's recommendations before the call with Nebula:

1) H100 vs A100 split: for p95 tail on streaming we should bias H100 to the front-line serving (~60% H100 / 40% A100 by slot weight). H100's Transformer kernels + faster FP8 paths give better single-stream latency at equivalent batch sizes.

2) Effective concurrency planning: assume continuous batching for embeddings with max batch = 128; for streaming chat plan for batch size 1–8. That means we need to isolate a small set of nodes (2–3) configured with aggressive preemption for low-concurrency streams.

3) Caching and prefix reuse: add a dedicated KV cache layer per availability zone — estimate reduces token compute by ~12–18% if customer prompts are templated. We should include a conservative 15% token-savings line in the workbook.

4) Multiplexing operational note: tenant packing will require per-tenant QoS and a runtime guardrail that prevents noisy neighbors from evicting KV cache. We should include a runbook step for emergency capacity expansion (API key toggle to force fallback to dedicated A100 pool).

I'll prepare a short slide with kernel/latency numbers for the call.

— Ava
Senior ML Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: Ravi Patel <ravi.patel@nebulasystems.com>, Susan Park <susan.park@nebulasystems.com>
Cc: ava_chen@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-29T14:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity questionnaire — initial data request

Ravi / Susan —

Confirmed for Aug 29 10:00 PT (we'll send a calendar invite). Quick answers inline and attached SLA table.

- Expected throughput per node (conservative on long sequences):
  • H100 (80GB): ~95–120 tokens/sec for single-stream-optimized kernels at 200-token avg with streaming enabled; up to 600 tokens/sec in batched embed mode.
  • A100-80GB: ~60–80 tokens/sec single-stream; 800–1,200 tokens/sec for dense batch embedding runs (batch=128).

- Burst pool recommendation: pre-reserve a nominal burst commitment (we recommend 50% of expected burst capacity) to guarantee short-notice availability, combined with on-demand credits to handle rare surges. This hybrid minimizes committed spend while keeping burst SLOs reliable.

- SLA table: attached nebula_sla_table.pdf — ties p95 latency targets and availability to service credits and automatic fallbacks. Two notable items: an automated model-fallback happens before credits are paid (to prioritize availability), and credits are only awarded for sustained SLO misses > 10 minutes.

Attachments: nebula_sla_table.pdf (SLA mapping + credit math). Also here's the HubSpot link to the draft deal and the Drive folder for our shared workbook: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/NEB-2026-0421 and https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-nebula-dedicated.

We'll walk through the kernel numbers and the workbook on the call and then iterate the final workbook by EOD.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Director, Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference
